body: surface-extraction-completeness-unrecorded: Evidence, re-verified, unchanged since filing: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:99 (Autonomous extraction) has the surface extractor write extraction.json as 'one entry per element the walk found', with each kind 'discovered by the walk, never pre-declared'; its rules (audit/SKILL.md:103-105) bound the walk ('goes no deeper than classification requires') and ask for no per-kind population source or count. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md:168 (Project) sets catalog population: to 'public members the extraction holds for this kind' and rows 'match the extraction's public side one-to-one'; SKILL.md:18 says this lets 'a reader trust that what is not in the catalog does not exist'. Mechanism: the catalog's completeness is checked only against the extraction, and the extraction records no population it enumerated from, so an element the walk missed is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, and no audit or check can refute the omission. Corpus: story:answer-absence-from-catalogs, 'every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population' -- 'enumerated population' is read either as the extraction's entries or as an exhaustive per-kind enumeration. concept:surface-extraction, 'one entry per element the walk found' and 'It states what the walk found and how the intent classified it -- nothing else', decides neither; artifact-definitions.md:358 ('Every universal comes back as a count and its population ... where the set came from') governs audit records, not the extraction, and is the nearest stated rule. Harm: a consuming agent answers 'does not exist' with false confidence; no accept-list entry is needed since this is a judgment issue. Options: A. Completeness relative to the extraction: catalog matches the extraction's public side one-to-one (already the skill text); amend concept:surface-extraction Boundaries to say the walk's exhaustiveness is not promised, and narrow the story's wording or leave it read that way. Cost: the story's 'with confidence ... without reading the source' rests on an unrefutable walk. B. Exhaustive enumeration: the extractor records per kind the population it enumerated from (the files, registries, or declarations it read) and its count, the catalog's population: rests on that record, and the audit can refute a missed element. Cost: the concept's 'nothing else' boundary widens, the extractor's 'no deeper than classification requires' bound changes, and runs cost more. C (filer missed): record the per-kind source the walk read without promising exhaustiveness, so a reader sees where the set came from (the artifact-definitions.md:358 shape) and the concept says only that; the story still reads as relative completeness. Cost: half-way; absence is checkable against a named source but not guaranteed. Tooling a fix edits: audit/SKILL.md Autonomous extraction (the extractor's rules), document/SKILL.md Project (population:), document/goal.md term 2, and the concept and possibly the story. Siblings to rule with: document-catalog-per-declared-kind and document-goal-skips-catalog-completeness, both routed defect; their fixes (a file per extraction kind, rows one-to-one with the extraction) hold under every option.

body: run-group-lends-terminal: Evidence, re-verified: the built reading is option A. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group:start (L309) calls foreground_terminal (L249), which checks fds 0, 1, and 2 (TERMINAL_FDS, L72), not input alone as the filed problem says; where one is a terminal whose foreground group is run-group's, run_lent (L296) hands the terminal to the run's group, and lent_wait (L279) takes it back and SIGSTOPs run-group itself when the command stops for any reason but a terminal read, so Ctrl-Z stops run-group as a shell job. The holder ignores SIGINT, SIGQUIT, and SIGTSTP (HOLD_CODE, L66). The reference doc plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md:214-221 documents this: 'start lends the terminal to the run's group ... Ctrl-C reaches every process of the group but the holder, and Ctrl-Z stops the command and run-group together.' The reference stack tool never meets it: scripts/stack runs the start command with stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL (L489) and its output to stack-start.log. So the case is an operator or a project's own command calling run-group start at a terminal. Mechanism: a server the command starts with a trailing & stays in the run's group (the group is what stop signals), so a Ctrl-C meant for the foreground command also reaches the server unless the server ignores SIGINT. Corpus: decision:stack-helpers-serve-project-commands ('The suite ships helpers a project may call from its own commands, each usable alone') and decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run (down 'stops the run's process group') fix that every process the run starts is in its group; neither says what an operator's terminal keystrokes reach. The corpus is silent on the terminal. Harm: no accept-list entry decides it; the option the owner picks narrows or widens what run-group promises an operator at a terminal. Options: A, keep lending (built and documented): Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z act on the whole run as a foreground job does, at the cost that Ctrl-C also ends a background server the operator meant to keep. B, refuse a terminal (the filer's B): run-group start refuses where fd 0, 1, or 2 is a terminal, or runs the command with input from /dev/null; cost: an interactive command (a prompt, a password read) cannot run under run-group, and an operator who runs it by hand must redirect. C, the filer's discarded reading, run the command outside the run's group: breaks stop, which signals the group, so it fails the corpus's 'stops the run's process group'; not a real option. D, missed by the filer: keep the command in the run's group but do not lend the terminal, so Ctrl-C reaches run-group alone (in the shell's group) and run-group forwards SIGINT to the command's pid only, leaving background members running until stop; cost: a terminal read by the command stops it with SIGTTIN, and a forwarding handler is new code. A choice other than A edits docs/stack-helpers.md and project.md's run-group entry in the same change. Siblings: none among the open records.

body: true-up-undecodable-review-facts-skipped: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:review_config_mode (L3692) reads .ok-planner/review/project.md (or .ok-review/project.md in check mode) with read_owner, and on UnicodeDecodeError (L3718) returns with no line printed, so neither the check step's 'stale:' line nor the fix step's rewrite of .ok-review/bin/review to .ok-planner/bin/review happens. The wording offer cannot catch it: wording_left (L2377) strips '.ok-review/bin/review' before stale_wording_lines (L2384) looks for a retired estate path, since review_config_mode owns that name. The stack-lines offer the fixer leans on is narrower than the filed problem says: stack_plan (L3227) lists 'it does not decode as UTF-8 ...' only where written_stack_lines(declaration) is non-empty, so a project whose .ok-planner/config.json declares no stack gets nothing, stack_lines_offers (L3281) drops it for a seeded skeleton, and even where it shows it names the decode failure, never the retired review-tool name. Mechanism: the file stays naming .ok-review/bin/review, which /converge pastes into every prompt, so agents told to run the review tool by that path meet a missing file once the retired estate is gone. Sibling idioms in the same core: the retired-script caller scan classifies an undecodable caller as kind 'encoding' (L1920-1921), described at L1801 as 'a file that does not decode as UTF-8, so true-up cannot rewrite it byte for byte', and files an intake issue for it (L2000); the retired-sections strip collects undecodable paths (L1482) rather than rewriting them. Corpus: decision:whole-file-ownership lets true-up rewrite 'a value in owner-declared configuration that names a retired estate's path ... with no offer' and, for a retired script line it cannot rewrite, says 'true-up files an intake issue for the owner and leaves the line'; it says nothing of undecodable files. decision:retired-script-repoint-needs-a-proven-root is about prefixes, not encodings. Stated rule: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md rule 4.6, 'A caught error never ends in a bare log line or a silent default', rules out the silent return at L3718, so option A as filed ('says nothing of it') is not compliant; the choice is among the rest. Options: A, skip and stay silent: breaks rule 4.6 and leaves projects with no stack declaration with no notice. B, rewrite the ASCII name byte for byte in the raw bytes: fixes the reference with no question, at the cost of a second idiom beside the core's never-rewrite-undecodable rule (L1801) and a wrong edit in an encoding where the ASCII bytes do not stand for the name, such as UTF-16. C, a cleanup offer for the file, as the caller scan's 'encoding' issue does: matches the sibling, at the cost of one more owner question on a rare file. D, missed by the filer: print a 'stale:' line naming the file and the retired name from both check and fix, with no offer and no write; cost: a notice the owner must act on unprompted, weaker than the sibling's intake issue. Siblings: none among the open records.

body: unread-counts-only-agent-messages: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:54 sets AGENT_TYPE_AUTHORS = {"reply": (TRIAGE,), "update": AGENT_AUTHORS}; issues:510 unread_message counts a message only where m["type"] is in AGENT_TYPE_AUTHORS; issues:502 agent_mark and issues:1213 (read) set the person's ledger mark to the highest agent message number, not the highest message. The dashboard counts through the same module, so 'issues list --unread' and 'GET /api/issues?unread=1' both skip a person's comment or ruling. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: a person's comment or ruling is never counted, and reading an issue records only the agent mark, so counting people's messages also needs the mark to cover every message and a person's own messages to be excluded by author name. Corpus: story:see-new-analysis 'have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'; decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner covers agent revisions only ('whichever ceremony writes it') and is silent on people's messages; decision:unread-issues-count-as-new counts a never-read issue as new 'whoever filed it'; decision:read-marks-kept-per-person keeps marks per person. Tooling text that states the current behavior: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:391 ('each triage reply, and every agent revision of a routed or ruled issue, stays unread to you') and .ok-planner/review/project.md's --unread line ('open issues with agent messages you have not read'). Harm: a second person's answer or ruling on an issue another person already read never shows as new to that person (A9 would cover the unread count if the story's reading A holds). Options: A. Count every message, people's included, as unread to each person other than its author, on the CLI and the dashboard: code change in scripts/issues (unread_message, the read mark, an author check) plus the CLAUDE.md template and project.md lines; cost: unread counts grow in a busy multi-person intake, and a person's own edits or withdrawals need a rule. B. Reword story:see-new-analysis so 'whoever wrote them' means whichever agent or ceremony; code stays; cost: a person's answer reaches another person only by rereading. C (filer missed): count people's rulings as unread to others but not their comments; cost: a third rule to explain, and a comment that answers a question still goes unseen. Siblings: none open.

body: document-dropped-type-document-lingers: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md:132 (Walk, Empty types) reads 'Propose keeping it ..., narrowing it, or dropping it'; SKILL.md:312 (Placement) reads 'Only declared targets are written: no path is touched that no type names'; SKILL.md:314 removes stamped documents no declared type produced only 'directly under' a folder target, so a dropped file-target type's document stays. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/goal.md:83-87 lists 'a document at a path no type targets' under Not met. SKILL.md:133 (Untyped documentation) raises such a file only at a later run's walk, and its 'drops the file as not documentation' removes nothing. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: the walk computes its deltas once, before the owner drops the type, and Placement may not touch the dropped target, so the run ends with a stamped document at an undeclared path; that document fails goal rule's Not met term in this run and in every later run until someone removes it by hand. Corpus: decision:documents-generated-per-type-and-placed 'Only declared types' targets are written' and 'Per-type targets are what make placement safe: nothing is overwritten that no type claims'; the same decision already carves one removal: the docs/ rules file, which the step 'removes ... once no type does'. story:ship-release-documents 'documentation that describes that release'. decision:placed-documents-are-records keeps a stale document as a record that files nothing. Harm: A3 (an owner action through /document leaves a state where later use fails: the goal never verifies), and a document stamped with an older release stays where readers look. Options: A. Placement removes the stamped document at the target of a type the walk dropped this release, as the folder sweep does under a folder target; cost: widens 'Only declared types' targets are written', so it needs a corpus delta to documents-generated-per-type-and-placed beside its rules-file removal clause. B. The walk, when the owner drops a file-target type whose target holds a stamped document, asks in the same message whether to remove that document, and removes it on the owner's word; cost: one more line in the walk's one message, and a kept file is then untyped documentation the next walk raises again. C. goal.md counts a stamped document at a path no type targets as met-despite; cost: the stale document stays where readers look with no owner ever asked. Siblings: none open.

converge-calls-reach-owner-as-counts: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:146 ('hunt') reports failures 'sorted defect, not-owed, environment, judgment, upstream, rejected' as counts; SKILL.md:148 ('fixed') reads 'defects verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck, by entry of the accept list or sprint class'; SKILL.md:150 ('intake') lists 'every report and failure the merge rejected as a record or a document the release regenerates, with its file' and, in sprint mode, 'every unlisted call', but no rejection as not real or not covered and no single-reading not-owed sort. The reasons live only in the ledger's notes under .ok-planner/review/runs/. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: a decline is set by a fixer and accepted by a verifier, and a not-owed sort or rejection is set by a merge agent, all with the owner absent; the return names them by count, so the owner who wants to overturn one must read the ledger. Corpus: story:veto-calls-made-in-my-absence 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with'; concept:completion-report records 'every call made where the sprint was silent' and 'what was decided in the owner's absence' for a sprint execution only; decision:skill-text-is-reviewed-as-code names a fixer that 'declines a fix' apart from one that 'records a question'; decision:converge-finds-then-fixes ('Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck') is silent on whether a decline is a call. The corpus does not define 'call'. Harm: an owner who disagrees with a decline or a not-owed sort cannot find it from the run's report; no accept-list entry decides it, since the story's word 'call' carries two readings. Options: A. Every judgment a /converge run makes alone is a call: the return lists each verified decline, each single-reading not-owed sort, and each rejection as not real or not covered, by site and reason; cost: a long return block in analysis runs, and converge/SKILL.md's return and merge prompts change. B. A call is the kind the suite records as a call (calls-pool items, triage's rulings and closes, a builder's calls); a corpus delta says so in the story or a concept, and declines, sorts, and rejections stay in the ledger; cost: the owner's veto of a decline needs a ledger read. C (filer missed): the return lists declines by site and reason, since a verifier accepted each against the owner's rules, and keeps sorts and rejections as counts with a pointer to the ledger file; cost: a split rule the owner must remember. Siblings: unread-counts-only-agent-messages turns on the same 'whoever/whatever' reading pattern but rules apart.

- i34: unread-counts-only-agent-messages: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:54 sets AGENT_TYPE_AUTHORS = {"reply": (TRIAGE,), "update": AGENT_AUTHORS}; issues:510 unread_message counts a message only where m["type"] is in AGENT_TYPE_AUTHORS; issues:502 agent_mark and issues:1213 (read) set the person's ledger mark to the highest agent message number, not the highest message. The dashboard counts through the same module, so 'issues list --unread' and 'GET /api/issues?unread=1' both skip a person's comment or ruling. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: a person's comment or ruling is never counted, and reading an issue records only the agent mark, so counting people's messages also needs the mark to cover every message and a person's own messages to be excluded by author name. Corpus: story:see-new-analysis 'have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'; decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner covers agent revisions only ('whichever ceremony writes it') and is silent on people's messages; decision:unread-issues-count-as-new counts a never-read issue as new 'whoever filed it'; decision:read-marks-kept-per-person keeps marks per person. Tooling text that states the current behavior: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:391 ('each triage reply, and every agent revision of a routed or ruled issue, stays unread to you') and .ok-planner/review/project.md's --unread line ('open issues with agent messages you have not read'). Harm: a second person's answer or ruling on an issue another person already read never shows as new to that person (A9 would cover the unread count if the story's reading A holds). Options: A. Count every message, people's included, as unread to each person other than its author, on the CLI and the dashboard: code change in scripts/issues (unread_message, the read mark, an author check) plus the CLAUDE.md template and project.md lines; cost: unread counts grow in a busy multi-person intake, and a person's own edits or withdrawals need a rule. B. Reword story:see-new-analysis so 'whoever wrote them' means whichever agent or ceremony; code stays; cost: a person's answer reaches another person only by rereading. C (filer missed): count people's rulings as unread to others but not their comments; cost: a third rule to explain, and a comment that answers a question still goes unseen. Siblings: none open.

SKILL.md:133 (Untyped documentation) raises such a file only at a later run's walk, and its 'drops the file as not documentation' removes nothing. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: the walk computes its deltas once, before the owner drops the type, and Placement may not touch the dropped target, so the run ends with a stamped document at an undeclared path; that document fails goal rule's Not met term in this run and in every later run until someone removes it by hand. Corpus: decision:documents-generated-per-type-and-placed 'Only declared types' targets are written' and 'Per-type targets are what make placement safe: nothing is overwritten that no type claims'; the same decision already carves one removal: the docs/ rules file, which the step 'removes ... once no type does'. story:ship-release-documents 'documentation that describes that release'. decision:placed-documents-are-records keeps a stale document as a record that files nothing. Harm: A3 (an owner action through /document leaves a state where later use fails: the goal never verifies), and a document stamped with an older release stays where readers look. Options: A. Placement removes the stamped document at the target of a type the walk dropped this release, as the folder sweep does under a folder target; cost: widens 'Only declared types' targets are written', so it needs a corpus delta to documents-generated-per-type-and-placed beside its rules-file removal clause. C (filer missed): the return lists declines by site and reason, since a verifier accepted each against the owner's rules, and keeps sorts and rejections as counts with a pointer to the ledger file; cost: a split rule the owner must remember. Mechanism: a person's comment or ruling is never counted, and reading an issue records only the agent mark, so counting people's messages also needs the mark to cover every message and a person's own messages to be excluded by author name. Corpus: story:see-new-analysis 'have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them'; decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner covers agent revisions only ('whichever ceremony writes it') and is silent on people's messages; decision:unread-issues-count-as-new counts a never-read issue as new 'whoever filed it'; decision:read-marks-kept-per-person keeps marks per person. Tooling text that states the current behavior: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:391 ('each triage reply, and every agent revision of a routed or ruled issue, stays unread to you') and .ok-planner/review/project.md's --unread line ('open issues with agent messages you have not read'). Harm: a second person's answer or ruling on an issue another person already read never shows as new to that person (A9 would cover the unread count if the story's reading A holds). Options: A. Count every message, people's included, as unread to each person other than its author, on the CLI and the dashboard: code change in scripts/issues (unread_message, the read mark, an author check) plus the CLAUDE.md template and project.md lines; cost: unread counts grow in a busy multi-person intake, and a person's own edits or withdrawals need a rule. B. Reword story:see-new-analysis so 'whoever wrote them' means whichever agent or ceremony; code stays; cost: a person's answer reaches another person only by rereading. C (filer missed): count people's rulings as unread to others but not their comments; cost: a third rule to explain, and a comment that answers a question still goes unseen. Siblings: none open.

document-dropped-type-document-lingers: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md:132 (Walk, Empty types) reads 'Propose keeping it ..., narrowing it, or dropping it'; SKILL.md:312 (Placement) reads 'Only declared targets are written: no path is touched that no type names'; SKILL.md:314 removes stamped documents no declared type produced only 'directly under' a folder target, so a dropped file-target type's document stays. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/goal.md:83-87 lists 'a document at a path no type targets' under Not met. SKILL.md:133 (Untyped documentation) raises such a file only at a later run's walk, and its 'drops the file as not documentation' removes nothing. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: the walk computes its deltas once, before the owner drops the type, and Placement may not touch the dropped target, so the run ends with a stamped document at an undeclared path; that document fails goal rule's Not met term in this run and in every later run until someone removes it by hand. Corpus: decision:documents-generated-per-type-and-placed 'Only declared types' targets are written' and 'Per-type targets are what make placement safe: nothing is overwritten that no type claims'; the same decision already carves one removal: the docs/ rules file, which the step 'removes ... once no type does'. story:ship-release-documents 'documentation that describes that release'. decision:placed-documents-are-records keeps a stale document as a record that files nothing. Harm: A3 (an owner action through /document leaves a state where later use fails: the goal never verifies), and a document stamped with an older release stays where readers look. Options: A. Placement removes the stamped document at the target of a type the walk dropped this release, as the folder sweep does under a folder target; cost: widens 'Only declared types' targets are written', so it needs a corpus delta to documents-generated-per-type-and-placed beside its rules-file removal clause. B. The walk, when the owner drops a file-target type whose target holds a stamped document, asks in the same message whether to remove that document, and removes it on the owner's word; cost: one more line in the walk's one message, and a kept file is then untyped documentation the next walk raises again. C. goal.md counts a stamped document at a path no type targets as met-despite; cost: the stale document stays where readers look with no owner ever asked. Siblings: none open.

converge-calls-reach-owner-as-counts: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:146 ('hunt') reports failures 'sorted defect, not-owed, environment, judgment, upstream, rejected' as counts; SKILL.md:148 ('fixed') reads 'defects verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck, by entry of the accept list or sprint class'; SKILL.md:150 ('intake') lists 'every report and failure the merge rejected as a record or a document the release regenerates, with its file' and, in sprint mode, 'every unlisted call', but no rejection as not real or not covered and no single-reading not-owed sort. The reasons live only in the ledger's notes under .ok-planner/review/runs/. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: a decline is set by a fixer and accepted by a verifier, and a not-owed sort or rejection is set by a merge agent, all with the owner absent; the return names them by count, so the owner who wants to overturn one must read the ledger. Corpus: story:veto-calls-made-in-my-absence 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with'; concept:completion-report records 'every call made where the sprint was silent' and 'what was decided in the owner's absence' for a sprint execution only; decision:skill-text-is-reviewed-as-code names a fixer that 'declines a fix' apart from one that 'records a question'; decision:converge-finds-then-fixes ('Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck') is silent on whether a decline is a call. The corpus does not define 'call'. Harm: an owner who disagrees with a decline or a not-owed sort cannot find it from the run's report; no accept-list entry decides it, since the story's word 'call' carries two readings. Options: A. Every judgment a /converge run makes alone is a call: the return lists each verified decline, each single-reading not-owed sort, and each rejection as not real or not covered, by site and reason; cost: a long return block in analysis runs, and converge/SKILL.md's return and merge prompts change. B. A call is the kind the suite records as a call (calls-pool items, triage's rulings and closes, a builder's calls); a corpus delta says so in the story or a concept, and declines, sorts, and rejections stay in the ledger; cost: the owner's veto of a decline needs a ledger read. C (filer missed): the return lists declines by site and reason, since a verifier accepted each against the owner's rules, and keeps sorts and rejections as counts with a pointer to the ledger file; cost: a split rule the owner must remember. Siblings: unread-counts-only-agent-messages turns on the same 'whoever/whatever' reading pattern but rules apart.

Mechanism: the catalog's completeness is checked only against the extraction, and the extraction records no population it enumerated from, so an element the walk missed is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, and no audit or check can refute the omission. ' on GET /), so only a browser exercises its controls; curl reaches only the routes. Siblings: none open. - i32: run-group-lends-terminal: Evidence, re-verified: the built reading is option A. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group:start (L309) calls foreground_terminal (L249), which checks fds 0, 1, and 2 (TERMINAL_FDS, L72), not input alone as the filed problem says; where one is a terminal whose foreground group is run-group's, run_lent (L296) hands the terminal to the run's group, and lent_wait (L279) takes it back and SIGSTOPs run-group itself when the command stops for any reason but a terminal read, so Ctrl-Z stops run-group as a shell job. The holder ignores SIGINT, SIGQUIT, and SIGTSTP (HOLD_CODE, L66). The reference doc plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md:214-221 documents this: 'start lends the terminal to the run's group ... Ctrl-C reaches every process of the group but the holder, and Ctrl-Z stops the command and run-group together.' The reference stack tool never meets it: scripts/stack runs the start command with stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL (L489) and its output to stack-start.log. Mechanism: a server the command starts with a trailing & stays in the run's group (the group is what stop signals), so a Ctrl-C meant for the foreground command also reaches the server unless the server ignores SIGINT. Corpus: decision:stack-helpers-serve-project-commands ('The suite ships helpers a project may call from its own commands, each usable alone') and decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run (down 'stops the run's process group') fix that every process the run starts is in its group; neither says what an operator's terminal keystrokes reach. The corpus is silent on the terminal. Harm: no accept-list entry decides it; the option the owner picks narrows or widens what run-group promises an operator at a terminal. Options: A, keep lending (built and documented): Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z act on the whole run as a foreground job does, at the cost that Ctrl-C also ends a background server the operator meant to keep. B, refuse a terminal (the filer's B): run-group start refuses where fd 0, 1, or 2 is a terminal, or runs the command with input from /dev/null; cost: an interactive command (a prompt, a password read) cannot run under run-group, and an operator who runs it by hand must redirect. C, the filer's discarded reading, run the command outside the run's group: breaks stop, which signals the group, so it fails the corpus's 'stops the run's process group'; not a real option. D, missed by the filer: keep the command in the run's group but do not lend the terminal, so Ctrl-C reaches run-group alone (in the shell's group) and run-group forwards SIGINT to the command's pid only, leaving background members running until stop; cost: a terminal read by the command stops it with SIGTTIN, and a forwarding handler is new code. A choice other than A edits docs/stack-helpers.md and project.md's run-group entry in the same change. Siblings: none among the open records. - i33: true-up-undecodable-review-facts-skipped: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:review_config_mode (L3692) reads .ok-planner/review/project.md (or .ok-review/project.md in check mode) with read_owner, and on UnicodeDecodeError (L3718) returns with no line printed, so neither the check step's 'stale:' line nor the fix step's rewrite of .ok-review/bin/review to .ok-planner/bin/review happens. Sibling idioms in the same core: the retired-script caller scan classifies an undecodable caller as kind 'encoding' (L1920-1921), described at L1801 as 'a file that does not decode as UTF-8, so true-up cannot rewrite it byte for byte', and files an intake issue for it (L2000); the retired-sections strip collects undecodable paths (L1482) rather than rewriting them. Corpus: decision:whole-file-ownership lets true-up rewrite 'a value in owner-declared configuration that names a retired estate's path ... with no offer' and, for a retired script line it cannot rewrite, says 'true-up files an intake issue for the owner and leaves the line'; it says nothing of undecodable files. decision:retired-script-repoint-needs-a-proven-root is about prefixes, not encodings. Options: A, skip and stay silent: breaks rule 4.6 and leaves projects with no stack declaration with no notice. B, rewrite the ASCII name byte for byte in the raw bytes: fixes the reference with no question, at the cost of a second idiom beside the core's never-rewrite-undecodable rule (L1801) and a wrong edit in an encoding where the ASCII bytes do not stand for the name, such as UTF-16. C, a cleanup offer for the file, as the caller scan's 'encoding' issue does: matches the sibling, at the cost of one more owner question on a rare file. D, missed by the filer: print a 'stale:' line naming the file and the retired name from both check and fix, with no offer and no write; cost: a notice the owner must act on unprompted, weaker than the sibling's intake issue.
